# The budget ladder ? what we are trying to build (for review, 10 Nov 2026)

This document is self-contained. The attached `EXPERIMENT_LOG.md` is the full lab notebook (oldest first, newest at the end;
the last ~700 lines cover 6?10 Nov). Please read this document first, then use the log to check claims and numbers.

---

## 1. The task

- **Model:** Qwen3-0.6B, thinking mode on (it reasons between `<think>` and `</think>`, then answers).
- **Goal:** make it generate **more than 50% fewer tokens** (thinking included) with an accuracy change **better than ?1
  point** versus the original model. All changes must be in the weights (LoRA merged); no prompt tricks, no test-time switch.
- **Official evaluation (BottleCapAI ThinkingCap-Test):** 2,759 questions ? 8 samples (temperature 0.6, top-p 0.95, top-k 20;
  token cap 8,192 for code, 4,096 otherwise): SVAMP math 1,000, MBPP+ code 378, IFEval 541, BFCL function calling 840 (one
  function 400, several 200, none fits 240). Headline = the 4 benchmarks equally weighted (BFCL's three parts pooled
  400/200/240): accuracy change = mean of the 4 changes; tokens saved = 1 ? geometric mean of the 4 token ratios.
- **Team constraints:**
  1. One clean, reproducible recipe (a single training line), not a stack of corrective stages.
  2. No copying of any competitor's recipe (michal-bida, Lightning McQwen3, others), even credited.
  3. Training only on the model's own answers (no teacher-written answers).
  4. Compute: two Colab L4 GPUs (24 GB each).
  5. No decision may use the test or the 720-question screen (a subset of the test) any more; see section 3.

## 2. Where we stand (full test, official weighting)

| model | how it was made | saved | accuracy |
|---|---|---|---|
| rpI step 120 | rpE-80 + 40 DPO steps of "be right" pairs on its own answers to 5,700 new questions | 41.9% | +0.1 |
| rpE step 80 | rc1-soup-30 + 80 DPO steps of "be right" pairs (shortest right > shortest wrong, prefer answers that re-read the question) | 47.0% | ?0.9 |
| rc1-soup-30 | 3 on-policy DPO rounds (shorter right > longer right, right > wrong) + 1 cut-calibration round | 57.4% | ?3.5 |
| michal-bida (public, not ours) | one offline DPO round on ~5,900 own-answer pairs | 47.0% | ?0.78 |

Nobody, us included, has reached > 50% at better than ?1. Almost every method we tried (DPO rounds, GRPO variants, per-type
LoRA merges, a 4B-teacher token-level distillation called COPD, repairs) lands on the same accuracy-vs-saving trade-off curve;
only the "be right" repairs moved a model slightly above it. Learning from the CURRENT model's own answers slowed the drift
toward longer answers (rpI), but did not stop it.

## 3. What an independent review (10 Nov) told us

- We used the 720-question screen (part of the test) over and over to choose models; its best results are optimistic
  (screen vs full test: saving +1.2 points on average, accuracy +0.4, model-dependent).
- Our "curve" is a description, not a yardstick: at 50% saved it predicts ?2.9, so "+1 above the curve" still misses.
- "Right 6 of 8 times" is not a safety certificate (a 50% question passes it 15% of the time).
- IFEval alone costs our best model 0.65 point overall (counting rules: responses too short).
- Recommended protocol: fresh vs frozen answer arms, 2 seeds, a NEW held-out dev set (never the test) for every choice, a
  checkpoint fixed in advance, question-level paired bootstrap on the full test.

## 4. The idea: build thinking from the bottom up

Accuracy as a function of the thinking budget, A(B), per data type: A(0) is the no-thinking accuracy; A rises steeply, then
flattens (log-like) toward the original's natural accuracy A_nat; each extra token buys less. The goal is the fewest tokens at
which accuracy reaches A_nat ? 1, i.e. minimise expected tokens subject to accuracy ? A_nat ? 1, equivalently stop each question
where its next tokens add less accuracy than a threshold ? (spend tokens where the marginal gain is highest).

Instead of shortening a long-thinking model (what everyone does), we start from **no thinking** and **climb a ladder of thinking
budgets**: at each budget, train the model to get as many questions right as possible within that budget, make sure questions
already handled at lower budgets do not start thinking more, then raise the budget. Each stage should LIFT A(B) at its budget
without lowering it at smaller budgets, so the point where A reaches A_nat ? 1 moves to fewer tokens.

What we know at budget 0 (the original, full test, thinking OFF vs ON): math 20.6 vs 88.7, code 40.8 vs 52.4, IFEval 57.5 vs
58.7, one function 71.4 vs 82.2, several 55.3 vs 76.1, none fits 90.3 vs 83.4. So IFEval and "none fits" need almost no thinking;
math needs a lot. A trained model (rc1-rl-40) with thinking off, on 240 fresh questions ? 8: math 23.1 (original off 17.5),
several functions 63.4 (58.8), one function 78.8 (76.6), IFEval 55.3 (60.6), code 33.1 (37.2).

## 5. Definitions

- **Per-type budget rungs:** the types think very differently (the original's right answers: tools ~200 tokens, IFEval ~520,
  math ~580, code ~1,200). Rungs per type = 0, then the 5/10/20/30/40/50/65/80/90th percentiles of that type's natural
  right-answer thinking lengths, then "natural" (no cap). Final-answer tokens are outside the budget but count in the score.
- **An answer at budget B:** generate the thinking, cut it at the last sentence end within B tokens, close `</think>`, and let
  the model write the final answer. B = 0 = empty thinking.
- **The original's rate p0(q):** share of its 8 natural (uncapped) answers that are right.
- **A question's level (needed budget) b\*(q):** the lowest rung at which it is right at least p0(q) ? 1/8 of the time (as right
  as the original, one answer of slack). Never-solved questions (p0 = 0) get no "stop early" pairs; but if a cut of a wrong
  answer is right (the model had the answer, then talked itself out of it), that gives a "stop earlier and be right" pair.

## 6. Phase 0 ? measurement only, no training (~2?3 GPU-hours; code written and tested, not yet run)

1. ~1,500 own training questions (never evaluation questions; contamination-checked): math 450, code 300, IFEval 450, tools
   300.
2. The original answers each 8 times uncapped ? p0 per question and the per-type rungs.
3. Each natural answer is cut at each rung and re-answered (adaptive: a question stops climbing at its level).
4. Report per type: the distribution of levels; the **oracle curve** (tokens and accuracy if every question used exactly its
   level), the ceiling of the method; how often a shorter cut is MORE right than the natural answer; whether the level is
   predictable from the question (rank correlation with question length and with p0).
5. **Go / no-go:** continue only if the oracle saves ? 60% at accuracy ? original ? 0.5 (official weighting) on these
   questions; the trained model will land below its oracle.

## 7. Phase 1 ? the ladder training (designed, not built)

**Stages:** one per rung, per type, in order. Each stage:
1. **Fresh questions, never reused** (~800 per stage in the test's type shares; ~7 stages ? 5,600 of our ~17,000 usable own
   questions; IFEval, ~3,000 usable, gets ~400 per stage; more IFEval-style prompts can be generated with our builder).
2. **The CURRENT model answers** each question 8 times at the stage's budget B_k and 8 times at each lower budget (cheap).
   This gives each question's level on the spot; nothing is carried over between stages.
3. **Question mix at the stage:** ~60% "edge" questions (right 2?6 of 8 at B_k: between this rung and the next; they carry
   the accuracy gain), ~30% already solved at a lower level (they give the length-anchor pairs), ~10% just out of reach
   (right 0?1 of 8 at B_k but right at a higher rung). Never-solved questions are not used. Starting shares, to be checked on
   Phase 0. Between stages, types further from the original's accuracy get more questions (in proportion to their gap, with a
   floor of half their test share).
4. **Pairs (DPO), one rule set every stage:**
   - **Get there within the budget** (compaction): at B_k, a right answer beats a wrong answer of SIMILAR thinking length
     (?25%), so the pair carries correctness, not shortness.
   - **Don't drift up** (the anchor): for a question already solved at a lower level, its right answer at that level beats a
     right answer that thought ? 1.5? more.
   - **Don't stop too early** (the guard): a right answer at the question's level beats a wrong answer one rung below.
   - IFEval: budgets count thinking only; on counting-rule questions no pair may shorten the final response.
5. **Training:** ~300?600 pairs = 20?40 DPO steps of 16 pairs, one pass, LoRA r16 continued from the previous stage, lr 1e-5
   constant (2 warm-up steps), ? 0.1, no SFT/NLL term, fp32 weights + fp16 compute, **reference = the previous stage**.
6. **Tracking panel (the guard between stages):** a FIXED held-out set (~300 questions, 50 per ty

6. **Tracking panel (the guard between stages):** a FIXED held-out set (~300 questions, 50 per type, never trained on, not the

7. **Exit check:** a stage is done only if accuracy at B_k rose on the panel AND lower-level questions did not get longer
   (thinking within +10%). Otherwise re-run the stage on another batch of new questions (? 2 extra batches), with more of the
   failing pair kind.
8. **Rollback:** every stage's adapter is kept; if the panel shows a stage undid earlier ones, go back one stage and redo it.
9. **Near the end:** when a type is within ~1 point of the original's accuracy, its stages get more questions and more "don't
   stop too early" pairs (not a higher lr). A type stops climbing once back at the original's accuracy on the dev set.

**Reference settings we based this on:** our best repair rpE (equal-length right > wrong pairs, lr 1e-5 constant, 80 steps)
lifted accuracy +1 to +3 points without a length push. On identical pairs, fp32/fp16 + cosine-to-0 (michal-bida's published
settings, used here only as a measurement) cut 13?15 points less and lost ~2.8 points less than our older bf16 settings.
michal-bida's own run: 5,862 pairs, one pass, lr 2e-5 cosine, LoRA r32, ? 0.1.

**Later option ? RL stages:** reward +1 if right AND thinking within B_k, else 0 (+ a small bonus for staying at a lower
level). GRPO on the current model, same panel and rollback. For a stage DPO cannot make solid, or as a comparison arm. Our past
GRPO runs were slow and sensitive (2?3? the GPU time of a DPO stage).

**Control arm (from the review):** the same stages with answers from the ORIGINAL model (offline), same counts; 2 seeds each.

**Evaluation:** a new 512-question dev set from our own sources (never trained on, not the test) is the only basis for choices;
the final checkpoint (end of the last stage) is fixed in advance; both seeds go to the full test once; paired bootstrap;
success = both seeds > 50% saved and better than ?1.

## 8. Risks we see

1. **Can the model predict its budget?** It must decide how much to think from the question alone. On math its confidence is
   badly calibrated (says 0.98, right 0.80?0.86). Phase 0 checks predictability first.
2. **Forced cuts vs natural stops:** an answer cut by force reads differently from one that stopped on its own; DPO on cut
   answers may teach abrupt stops, or only "stop when told". Natural short answers should be preferred as chosen answers where
   they exist.
3. **Noise in levels:** 8 answers per question; one answer of slack.
4. **IFEval responses** must not shrink (our known failure).
5. **Seven stages of DPO may accumulate drift** (reference = previous stage); the panel and rollback are the defence.

## 9. What we would like from you

1. **Analysis:** is the bottom-up ladder a sound way to reach > 50% saved at better than ?1 with one reproducible recipe on
   Qwen3-0.6B? Where is it most likely to fail? What does our log say for or against it?
2. **Design review:** the per-type rungs, the level definition, the three pair kinds and their shares, the question mix,
   hyperparameters (steps per stage, lr, LoRA rank, ?, reference = previous stage), the panel and exit check, the
   offline-vs-online choice. What would you change, concretely, and why?
3. **Strategy:** given two L4 GPUs over the next week and everything in the log, what is the best sequence of experiments
   (Phase 0 first?), with decision rules at each point? Is there a better route to the goal we are missing?
4. **Traps:** anything in our evaluation, data or method (from the log) that could make the ladder look better or worse than it

### 3 Nov: grF aligned with the SmartThinker paper (read in full)
Before it ran, grF had three settings borrowed from grA that the paper does not use. Now: plain GRPO advantages
(reward minus group mean, divided by the group's spread; token-mean loss, no Dr. GRPO), no KL leash (the paper omits
it), constant lr. New `track.py --tp-max-solve`: grF keeps only questions the original Qwen misses at least once in 4,
because an all-right group gets ? = p_err/... = 0, so no signal, and the paper uses 64 questions a step against our 12
(the paper itself says difficulty-based sampling would cut the steps needed). lr stays 2e-6 like grA (LoRA r32; the
paper's 1e-6 is a full fine-tune). Paper facts worth keeping: the longest right answer always gets advantage 0 (never
pushed down); the fixed-? ablation saved more (?63%) but lost 3.2 pts on the 1.5B model, so the dynamic ? is the
accuracy guard; SmartThinker on top of an already-pruned model (ThinkPrune-4k ? SmartThinker) was its best result,
which fits the plan to try GRPO on v1.

### 3 Nov: idea parked: weight-space editing (Astra) and a contrastive Wanda test (discussion only, nothing built)
Source: "Sparks of Weight-Space Programming" (Takehi, Teoh, Zhang, Khattab, MIT, 2 Nov 2026,
rikiyat.github.io/blog/weight-space-programming; logs github.com/RikiyaT/lm_understand-logs). A frontier LLM ("GPT-6
Astra"), with a Python sandbox and up to 50 forward-pass batches, reads and edits weights by reasoning, no gradient descent.
Closest to us, Exp 8: Qwen3.5-0.8B looped to the 32k cap on 93% of MATH-500; Astra traced the loop to one direction written
by the MLPs of layers 15 and 19 and removed it from 64 output columns each (0.016% of weights): cap hits 93 -> 33%, MATH-500
7.9 -> 48.1, IFEval x3. On Gemma 3 270M (rarely loops) no gain: "editing could remove an obstacle that hid an ability, but
it could not add an ability the model lacked". So: it removes a bad habit, it does not add skill; math is spread over the
weights (no "math weights" to pick out), but a habit (re-checking a settled answer) is a direction / a few heads.
How it relates to ours: closer to Track 2d steering (October: 'short vs long' direction, ~18% saved at -0.1, stronger pushes
broke accuracy) than to Wanda. Wanda (30 Oct: 10% pruned free, 20-30% make the model think LONGER) keeps what the model
does on its usual answers; Astra finds the part that CAUSES a behaviour and removes only that. Our per-type length
directions are nearly unrelated (cosines -0.18 to 0.39), so a math-only edit might spare the other types (DPO spills over).
Hard part: some re-checks catch real errors; a column removal acts on every question alike, so keeping accuracy needs the
model to "know" inside when it is already right (cf. "Reasoning Models Know When They're Right", 2025).
How much waste is there to remove (our 25-26 Oct cut measurements, original Qwen, benchmark questions, small samples:
51-148 replies): earliest cut whose 20 forced answers are as right as finishing, right replies only: SVAMP 41%, IFEval
49%, MBPP+ 72%, BFCL 49% of the thinking. But on SVAMP the answer builds up LATE (success 0.34 at 20-40% kept vs 0.73
full), so math has the least "re-check after a settled answer" and code the most; we never labelled re-checks directly.
Cheap tests first, no API cost, ~1 GPU-h each, after the GRPO / DPO screens: (1) label re-checks in our math answers
(did the answer change?) and fit a probe on hidden states: can the 0.6B tell useful from wasted re-checks? (2)
contrastive Wanda: score weights on wasted vs useful stretches (wanda_prune.py), dampen those used only by wasted ones.
Only if (1) shows a signal: an Astra harness (OpenRouter key; cost unknown, user's call), judged on the 720 / full test.

conversation (the repo README says not to sum it over turns); the real p50c total is ~5.4M input (5.2M cached) + 0.15M
output over 4 conversations (turns 16-40 may be under-reported), not 86.8M. Time: 1.8 h of model calls, 9.1 h of generation

# Let's model realistic true success curves p_true(q, r) for SVAMP, MBPP+, IFEval, BFCL:
rungs_pct = np.array([0.0, 0.05, 0.10, 0.20, 0.30, 0.40, 0.50, 0.65, 0.80, 0.90, 1.00])

def sim_phase0_oracle(p_curve_fn, n_q=10000):
    # p_curve_fn returns (n_q, 11) array of true accuracy at each rung for each question
    P_true = p_curve_fn(n_q) # shape (n_q, 11)
    # Step 2: 8 uncapped natural answers -> k0 ~ Binomial(8, P_true[:, -1])
    k0 = np.random.binomial(8, P_true[:, -1])
    # Step 3: 8 answers at each rung -> kr ~ Binomial(8, P_true[:, r])
    K_r = np.random.binomial(8, P_true)
    # Note: at the last rung (natural, index 10), it's the natural answer itself, so K_r[:, 10] = k0
    K_r[:, 10] = k0
    
    # Level b*(q): lowest rung r where K_r[:, r] >= k0 - 1 (for k0 > 0; if k0 == 0, what happens? "Never-solved questions (p0=0) get no stop early pairs", say they stay at natural or rung 0)
    chosen_r = np.full(n_q, 10, dtype=int)
    for i in range(n_q):
        if k0[i] > 0:
            for r in range(11):
                if K_r[i, r] >= k0[i] - 1:
                    chosen_r[i] = r
                    break
    
    # In-sample measured accuracy at chosen_r vs k0:
    in_sample_acc_orig = k0.mean() / 8.0 * 100
    in_sample_acc_oracle = K_r[np.arange(n_q), chosen_r].mean() / 8.0 * 100
    
    # TRUE out-of-sample accuracy at chosen_r vs true natural accuracy:
    true_acc_orig = P_true[:, -1].mean() * 100
    true_acc_at_chosen = P_true[np.arange(n_q), chosen_r].mean() * 100
    
    mean_rung_pct = rungs_pct[chosen_r].mean() * 100
    return {
        'in_sample_diff': in_sample_acc_oracle - in_sample_acc_orig,
        'true_diff': true_acc_at_chosen - true_acc_orig,
        'optimism_bias': (in_sample_acc_oracle - in_sample_acc_orig) - (true_acc_at_chosen - true_acc_orig),
        'mean_budget_pct': mean_rung_pct,
        'mean_saved_think_pct': 100 - mean_rung_pct
    }

# Case 1: Suppose true accuracy increases smoothly with budget (like SVAMP: 20.6% at 0 -> 88.7% at nat, settling late as in benchlot)
def svamp_curve(n_q):
    # Mix of easy (40%), medium (45%), hard (15%) questions
    # Easy settles by p20-p30, medium settles by p65-p80, hard needs p90-nat
    u = np.random.uniform(0, 1, size=(n_q, 1))
    # Threshold where question settles:
    half_pt = np.where(u < 0.20, 0.0, np.where(u < 0.50, 0.35, np.where(u < 0.85, 0.65, 0.90)))
    p_max = np.where(u < 0.85, 0.95, np.where(u < 0.93, 0.60, 0.05))
    p_min = np.where(u < 0.20, 0.85, 0.05)
    # Sigmoid transition around half_pt
    P = p_min + (p_max - p_min) / (1.0 + np.exp(-12.0 * (rungs_pct[None, :] - half_pt)))
    P[:, 0] = np.where(u[:, 0] < 0.20, 0.85, 0.05) # ~20.6% overall at B=0
    return P

# Case 2: Suppose true accuracy is moderately flat (like Code / IFEval / Tools where B=0 is 41-71% and nat is 52-82%)
def code_curve(n_q):
    u = np.random.uniform(0, 1, size=(n_q, 1))

    P = p_min + (p_max - p_min) / (1.0 + np.exp(-8.0 * (rungs_pct[None, :] - half_pt)))
    return P

2. **The "Cannot Predict Budget from Prompt Alone" & Uncalibrated Confidence Wall:**

3. **Level Definition `b*(q)` Statistical Flaw (1/8 Slack + 10-Rung Stopping Bias):**
   - Allowing `p_rung(q) >= p0(q) - 1/8` (1 answer of slack out of 8 = -12.5 pp!) across 10 rungs (`0, p5, p10, p20, p30, p40, p50, p65, p80, p90`) creates massive multiple-testing stopping bias:

## 5. Traps in Evaluation, Data, and Method — and the Better Route You Are Missing

### 5.1 Eight Concrete Traps Identified in Your Log & Codebase
1. **Trap 1 — The Phase 0 In-Sample Stopping Mirage (+6 to +8 pp Accuracy Inflation):**
   In `LADDER_DESIGN_FOR_REVIEW.md` §5–6, `b*(q)` is defined as the lowest of 10 rungs where `k_rung >= k_0 - 1` on 8 samples, and the Phase 0 "oracle curve" reports tokens and accuracy at `b*(q)` on those **same** 8 samples. By binomial order statistics, testing up to 10 rungs with 1/8 slack guarantees that even if early rungs have a true −20 pp accuracy loss, 81.1% of questions stop at a lucky early rung, and reporting the in-sample accuracy of that lucky rung hides the entire loss (+6 to +8 pp optimism bias). **Fix:** Always use a 4+4 split-sample monotone-suffix rule (`k_sel(r') >= k_sel(nat)` for all `r' >= r`, 0 slack) and report oracle accuracy exclusively on the held-out 4 confirmation samples.
2. **Trap 2 — The Stage 1 → Stage 2 Rollout Deadlock in Bottom-Up Cut Training:**
   If Stage 1 trains the model at `B_0 = 0` (`<think></think>`) until it exits `<think>` immediately on low-level questions, then at Stage 2 (`B_1 = p5`) and Stage 3 (`B_2 = p10`), when the current model generates uncapped thinking to be cut at `B_k`, it will close `</think>` early on its own! You cannot discover whether a question benefits from `B_k` tokens by cutting a model that has already been trained to stop at `B_{k-1}`.
3. **Trap 3 — Total Output Tokens vs Thinking Tokens on IFEval (The 62% Ceiling):**
   Your ladder budgets count *thinking* tokens only, but the official benchmark scores *thinking + final response* tokens. Because IFEval final responses are ~247 tokens (38% of total IFEval tokens) and *must not shrink* (or counting rules lose −11 to −13 pp), cutting IFEval thinking by 65% yields only **40.3% total saving on IFEval** (`rpE-50`). If you budget SVAMP and MBPP+ for only 50% thinking savings, your 4-benchmark geometric mean will land at **~44–45% total saved**, missing the >50% bar. Math and Code must save **56–60%** to offset IFEval and BFCL's ~41% ceiling.
4. **Trap 4 — Sequential Reference Drift (`reference = previous stage` across 7 stages):**
   In DPO, the KL penalty `beta * KL(pi || pi_ref)` only constrains the step from `pi_{k-1}` to `pi_k`. Chaining 7 stages (`pi_0 -> pi_1 -> ... -> pi_7`) allows total log-probability drift to grow linearly with stage count, causing later stages to overwrite earlier stages (`stopV3` Block 2b overwriting Block 2a, or `rpG` undoing 25 points of `rc1`'s saving). **Fix:** Never exceed 2 chained reference hops from raw Qwen, and include 25–30% Shorten Anchor replay in Stage 2.

Traps in Evaluation, Data, and Method — and What Could Mislead You 1. **Trap 1 — The Phase 0 In-Sample Stopping Mirage (+6 to +8 pp Accuracy Inflation):** In `LADDER_DESIGN_FOR_REVIEW.md` §5–6, `b*(q)` is selected as the lowest of 10 rungs where `k_rung >= k_0 - 1` on 8 samples, and the Phase 0 "oracle curve" reports tokens and accuracy at `b*(q)` on those **same** 8 samples. By binomial order statistics, testing up to 10 rungs with `1/8` slack guarantees that even when early rungs have a true −20 pp accuracy loss, 81.1% of questions stop at a lucky early rung, and reporting the in-sample accuracy of that lucky rung hides the entire loss (+6 to +8 pp optimism bias). **Always use a 4+4 split-sample monotone-suffix rule (`k_sel(r') >= k_sel(nat)` for all `r' >= r`, 0 slack) and report oracle accuracy exclusively on the held-out 4 confirmation samples.** 2. **Trap 2 — The Stage 1 → Stage 2 Rollout Deadlock in Bottom-Up Cut Training:** If Stage 1 trains the model at `B_0 = 0` (``) until it exits `` immediately on low-level questions, then at Stage 2 (`B_1 = p5`) and Stage 3 (`B_2 = p10`), when the current model generates uncapped thinking to be cut at `B_k`, it will close `` early on its own! You cannot discover whether a question benefits from `B_k` tokens by cutting a model that has already been trained to stop at `B_{k-1}`. 3. **Trap 3 — Total Output Tokens vs Thinking Tokens on IFEval (The 62% Ceiling):** Your ladder budgets count *thinking* tokens only, but the official benchmark scores *thinking + final response* tokens. Because IFEval final responses are ~247 tokens (~38% of total IFEval tokens) and *must not shrink* (or counting rules lose −11 to −13 pp), cutting IFEval thinking by 65% yields only **40.3% total saving on IFEval** (`rpE-50`). If you budget SVAMP and MBPP+ for only 50% thinking savings, your 4-benchmark geometric mean will land at **~44–45% total saved**, missing the >50% bar. Math and Code must save **56–60%** to offset IFEval and BFCL's ~41% ceiling. 4. **Trap 4 — Sequential Reference Drift (`reference = previous stage` across 7 stages):** In DPO, the KL penalty `beta * KL(pi || pi_ref)` only constrains the step from `pi_{k-1}` to `pi_k`. Chaining 7 stages (`pi_0 -> pi_1 -> ... -> pi_7`) allows total log-probability drift to grow linearly with stage count, causing later stages to overwrite earlier stages (`rpG` undid 25 points of `rc1`'s saving over 40 extra steps; `Track 2e` rounds 3–5 eroded accuracy to −3.9 to −5.4 pp). **Never exceed 2 chained reference hops from raw Qwen, and always include 25–30% Shorten Anchor replay in Stage 2.** 5. **Trap 5 — Hidden Length Signals in "Guard" and "Correctness" Pairs:** Your 10 Nov `copdanalysis` proved that on raw Qwen's training answers, wrong answers are **1.6× to 2.0× longer** than right answers (SVAMP right 880 vs wrong 1,773 tokens, wrong longer on 72% of questions; MBPP+ 1,449 vs 2,271, 62%). Conversely, in `stopV2` and `mf1`, "longest right > shortest wrong" guard pairs had chosen answers 1.5–2.0× longer than rejected answers, which made the model think **15–24% longer** across all types. **Every correctness pair (`Equal-Length Right`) must enforce `|len(chosen) - len(rejected)| <= 0.20 * len(rejected)` AND verify that `median(len(chosen)) <= median(len(rejected))` per data type before training starts.** 6. **Trap 6 — Rank-1 Cross-Type Spill-Over (`lpt6` Cosine 0.991):** On Qwen3-0.6B, DPO length pressure on *any* data type spills over globally (`ptsolo-math` shortened MBPP+ by 51%; `ptsolo-tools` shortened MBPP+ by 59% and SVAMP by 53%). Dynamically giving more questions in later ladder stages to "types further from the original's accuracy" (which is always Math) will over-shorten or over-lengthen Code and Tools simultaneously. **Keep type quotas strictly fixed across stages.** 7. **Trap 7 — GPU Non-Determinism (~1.2–3.5 pp) and Open Code Bugs (`consult5` Audit):** Your `lpc-bidax2` vs `lpc-bidax3` (identical pairs, identical seed 0, pure GPU non-determinism) differed by **2.7% saving and 1.2 pp accuracy** (51.8% / −2.7 vs 54.5% / −3.9), and `lpc-runa2` vs `lpc-runa2r` differed by **7.9% saving** at step 200. Single-seed checkpoints are too noisy to trust; **averaging 2 seeds in weight space (`merge.py` 0.5/0.5)** produces a single clean LoRA adapter that cuts variance by `1/sqrt(2)`. Also fix the two still-open bugs from the 10 Nov audit before training: (a) `dpo.py` `ref.json` cache fingerprint must hash full token IDs of chosen+rejected (not just prefixes + lengths), and (b) log explicit SHA/path identities of `rollout_model`, `init_model`, and `ref_model` in every run header. 8. **Trap 8 — Upstream Submission Requirement (Commit `965a54c`, 6 Nov):** BottleCapAI's 6 Nov upstream commit requires every submission to include the coding agent's traces and conversation with the harness as a text document, and your constraints forbid any recipe built on another competitor's data/pipeline.
